name_note: Enterocloster was proposed in 2020 for species previously named Clostridium, so most genomes in this GTDB genus appear in older papers as Clostridium bolteae, C. clostridioforme and relatives.

sentences.text: Enterocloster is a genus proposed for a clade of misclassified Clostridium species that sits phylogenetically inside the family Lachnospiraceae.
The clade renamed Enterocloster includes the former Clostridium clostridioforme, Clostridium bolteae, Clostridium citroniae and Clostridium lavalense.
Its family, Lachnospiraceae, is described as made up of benign gut microbiome members with plant-degrading capabilities.
Antibiotics are reported to compromise PD-1 blockade in cancer patients, and regrowth of Enterocloster species after antibiotics drove immunosuppressive T cells towards tumours.
A study reported Enterocloster bolteae enriched in patients with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis.
